Why Operations Experience Translates Directly to Data Analytics

Over the past 5+ years at Amazon India (~4.5 years across Selling Partner Support, T4 Escalation Investigations, and PSAS Operations Support), Teleperformance (14 months in AI Data Quality Evaluation), and BharatPe (3 months), my daily work has centered on diagnosing why operational defects happen and how to resolve them under strict SLAs.

  • → From Single Tickets to Systemic Trends: Investigating 35 to 40+ daily cases taught me how to trace root causes across order logs, fulfillment records, and policy SOPs.
  • → Data Quality & Structured Tagging: 14 months evaluating AI outputs in LRL and IHAL workflows built strong habits in data validation, defect categorization, and rubric compliance.
  • → Honest Technical Progression: I am actively rebuilding and demonstrating my analytical toolkit through completed projects in Excel, SQL, and Python, while developing my Power BI dashboarding skills.

Transferable Operations Core

  • • Escalation & Root-Cause Investigation: Auditing multi-step case histories and seller/warehouse evidence.
  • • SOP Research & Policy Compliance: Translating complex operational guidelines into accurate decisions.
  • • SLA & Queue Governance: Prioritizing high-volume ticket queues to sustain 90%–95% resolution benchmarks.
  • • Audit-Ready Documentation: Writing clear, structured investigation summaries and Excel tracking logs.

03 // Analytical Evidence & Deliverables

Data Analytics Projects

Three completed projects (Excel, SQL, Python) with real downloadable files and verified findings, plus one clearly labeled planned Power BI dashboard.

Synthetic Data Disclaimer: All project analyses use a 250-row synthetic e-commerce support ticket dataset (synthetic_operations_tickets_250rows.csv) and do not represent actual Amazon or employer performance.
Project 01 • Microsoft Excel Completed

Excel Operations & SLA Performance Analysis

Objective: Audit 250 synthetic support tickets (11 columns) using Excel helper formulas and summary tables to isolate SLA bottlenecks across issue categories and support tiers.

  • 85.6% Overall SLA Compliance (214 Within SLA, 36 Breached), 18.8 hrs average resolution time, and 96.8% QA pass rate.
  • Primary Bottleneck: Tier 2 Operations Support recorded 77.8% SLA compliance (31.5 hrs avg), while Fulfillment Discrepancies averaged 28.2 hrs.
IF / COUNTIF / COUNTIFS AVERAGEIF KPI Dashboard
Project 02 • SQL (SQLite3) Completed

SQL Business & Operations Case Analysis

Objective: Query the 250-row support_tickets relational table using GROUP BY and CASE WHEN to evaluate category turnaround and tier SLA compliance.

  • Fastest Queue: Order Status Inquiries averaged 7.1 hrs (91.5% SLA across 47 tickets).
  • Complex Escalations: Account Policy Escalations averaged 28.9 hrs (82.2% SLA), while Tier 1 absorbed 55.6% of total volume (139/250).
SELECT / WHERE / GROUP BY CASE WHEN COUNT / AVG / ROUND
Project 03 • Python (Pandas & Matplotlib) Completed

Python Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)

Objective: Inspect the 250-row synthetic ticket log with pandas to verify null counts, summarize FCR and category volume, and plot tier SLA performance against the 85.0% benchmark.

  • Data Hygiene & FCR: Confirmed 0 missing values across all 11 columns and a 57.6% First Contact Resolution rate (144/250).
  • Benchmark Variance: Plotted Tier 1 (+4.2 pts above 85% target), Tier 4 (-1.7 pts), and Tier 2 (-7.2 pts).
pandas.read_csv groupby().agg() matplotlib.pyplot
Wireframe Specification (Not a Completed Report)
Project 04 • Power BI Desktop Planned

Power BI Service Operations Dashboard

Planned Scope: Interactive Power BI Desktop dashboard built on the 250-row synthetic dataset to filter SLA compliance, backlog, and QA pass rates by Priority_Level and Merchant_Region.

  • Prepared Architecture: Power Query data-type rules and foundational DAX measures (COUNTROWS, CALCULATE, DIVIDE) documented.
